The per‑window errors are all negative and relatively close together, indicating stability. While the trimmed‑mean strategy is also stable, the weighted approach benefits from explicitly down‑weighting models with higher error, which is advantageous when the ranking is only moderately stable (Kendall tau ≈0.36).
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A (trimmed‑mean pool2) is slightly worse in overall score and its per‑window spread is larger, suggesting less robustness to window shifts. Candidate C (mean pool1) performs the worst among the three and has a larger gap to the best score; its per‑window errors are more variable, indicating poorer generalization. Thus, B is the preferred choice despite the higher variance risk, because the weighted scheme aligns with the series’ characteristics and shows the most consistent performance across validation windows.
